narrative.overview:
Clinical but humane. The page is a daylit rehab room painted in CSS: a eucalyptus wall meets a plaster floor at a level horizon, and a clay-soft figure sits at the four-target mat in front of it, rendered in a transparent React Three Fiber canvas laid over that painted room. The instrument is the hero. A plaster readout plate on the wall shows the live trunk angle and the limit, and the measurement stays the sharpest thing on screen so the room never reads as a wellness app.

Colour is quiet and committed. Wall green and deep forest own whole regions: the sticky stage is wall, the evidence band is drenched in forest, the close sits on wall. Terracotta isn't part of the palette at rest. It is a state. When the trunk holds past the limit (10°, for at least 200 ms, the same rule as the firmware) the room's light warms, a warm glow rises from the figure, and the readout turns terracotta. When the lean ends, all of it goes away.

Type pairs an upright Literata for display with Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for reading, and its Mono for every measured number. Density is low: one idea per viewport in the story, generous section padding after it.
keyCharacteristics: A painted room (wall over plaster floor, horizon at 78%) behind a transparent 3D canvas
Matte clay figure and ceramic mat, soft daylight, soft floor shadows
Terracotta appears only as the flagged-lean state, never as decoration
Every number is set in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular figures
Clean vs compensated is always an icon plus a label, never colour alone
Forest-drenched and wall-drenched full-width passages rather than cards
The therapist dashboard is Rehab Studio at working density: forest top bar, flat paper panels, one shared rep mark and one dashed limit in every chart

rules.name: The Terracotta Is a State Rule
rules.body: Terracotta appears only while something is past the limit, or as the mark of a rep that was. A surface at rest has no terracotta on it.

rules.name: The Stage Ink Rule
rules.body: Copy over the stage (wall or the painted room) is always forest. Muted ink appears only on plaster.

rules.name: The Small Terracotta Rule
rules.body: Terracotta text below large size uses terra-deep. Plain terra is for large readouts, glows and marks.

rules.name: The Warm Room Rule
rules.body: The flagged state tints the room itself, not just a badge. The wall mixes in 9% terra and the floor 6% (in oklab), through the registered `--room-wall` / `--room-floor` properties over 500ms ease-out. The 3D lights warm with it: sky, ground and key light lerp toward warm values.

rules.name: The Measured Number Rule
rules.body: Any number the device measures, or any limit it applies (angles, limits, percentages on axes, chart ticks), is set in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Upright Display Rule
rules.body: Literata headlines are always roman, never italic, at weight 500.

rules.name: The Forest-Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted with forest (rgb 31 45 39), never neutral black, and only the instrument and the primary action cast them.

rules.name: The Measured Terracotta Rule
rules.body: On the dashboard, terracotta appears in exactly these places: the filled diamond of a compensated rep, the compensated-share bar in the sessions table (it encodes that share, so it is a mark; decision 2026-11-19), compensated values (terra for large readouts such as a compensated rep's peak lean or the replay's live angle past the limit; terra-deep for small text such as a compensated row's peak lean), the replay playhead dot while past the limit, and the 3D replay trunk while past the limit. Nothing at rest is terracotta.

rules.name: The Direction In Words Rule
rules.body: A change between sessions is a signed Mono delta, a direction icon (ArrowDown, ArrowUp, or Minus when about the same) and words ("fewer compensated", "less lean", "slower"). Better is eucalyptus, worse is terra-deep, about the same is forest-2. Colour never carries the direction alone.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Exception
rules.body: On the dashboard only, content sits in panels: panel fill, a 1px wall hairline, 12px radius, no shadow, 20px padding (24px from sm on the Progress panels), or none for tables, which clip to the radius. This is the one place the "avoid cards" stance yields, and it yields to flat paper, not lifted cards. Tables inside panels divide rows with wall hairlines at 70% alpha.

rules.name: The One Mark Rule
rules.body: A rep is drawn the same way in every chart, strip and table cell by one shared mark: a clean rep is an open circle (panel fill, 1.8px forest stroke), a compensated rep a filled terracotta diamond (with a thin panel edge). Shape tells clean from compensated before colour does.

rules.name: The One Limit Rule
rules.body: The limit is a 1.5px forest line dashed 6/5 in every plot: the rep strip, the per-target scatter, the trend's lean view and the trunk trace. The legend's swatch uses the same dash.

dos: Do keep terracotta behind the flagged state: readout value and border in terra, the state line in terra-deep, the room tint at 9% (wall) and 6% (floor) terra, the glow at 0.17 alpha.
Do pair every clean or compensated signal with an icon and a word (CircleCheck "Within the limit", CircleX "Compensated").
Do set every measured number and limit in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular figures.
Do keep copy over the stage in forest (#1f2d27). Use muted ink (#4a5a52) only on plaster.
Do tint shadows with forest, and keep them for the primary button and the readout plate.
Do label simulated data in the caption every time it appears.
Do keep reduced motion working: no smooth scroll, no transitions, and the scene still responds to direct input. Without WebGL, the 2D SVG figure follows the same lean rule.
donts: Don't use terracotta as an accent, a link colour or a decoration on a surface at rest.
Don't set eucalyptus or terracotta as small text on the wall (3.6:1 and 3.2:1). On the wall, use them for strokes and large type only.
Don't set Literata headlines in italic or above weight 500. The wordmark is the one exception, at 600.
Don't put muted ink over the painted stage.
Don't wrap sections in shadowed cards. Use full-bleed bands and hairlines.
